simple.meaning: דּוּר (dûwr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a circle , ball or pile.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 3 times in Isaiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Isaiah 22:18. The surrounding contexts include flock.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דּוּר (H1754) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: דּוּר (dûwr) / H1754 is traced through Isaiah 22:18, Isaiah 29:3, Ezekiel 24:5 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He will surely wind you around and around, and throw you like a ball into a large country. There you will die, and there the chariots of your glory will be, you shame of your lord’s house.

definitions.full: H1754. dur דּוּר noun [masculine] circle, ball — 1 circle : Du Isa 29:3 thinks noun here also is כַּדּוּר (or כִּדּוֺר ) = כִּידוֺר onset of combatants ; Marti כְּדָוִד as ᵐ5 Lo Brd and others; עליך כַּדּוּר וְחָנִיתִי 29:3 ( > ᵐ5 Brd כְּדָוִד ). 2 ball כַּדּוּר צְנֵפָה יִצְנָפְךָ צָנוֺף Isa 22:18 (so most; but Bö NÄ ii. 134 De Or Jastr PAOS 1888, xciv ff. regard noun as כַּדּוּר , ball , as Talmud, compare also MV SS under the word; see כדר ).
